analyst_view.overall: Sunderland (11th, 7 pts) host Jagiellonia (29th, 3 pts) needing a win to stay in the play-off places, but Régis Le Bris's side are 19th in the Premier League and host Tottenham three days later, so heavy rotation is likely (they have kept only about a third of the XI across recent games). Sunderland are without Brian Brobbey (thigh), Granit Xhaka (calf), Habib Diarra, Daniel Ballard and Romaine Mundle, none of whom the numbers list; only Trai Hume's ban is counted. Jagiellonia, under Adrian Siemieniec, lost 3-1 at Cracovia on Saturday, have one European win, lose captain Taras Romanczuk to a ban, and their fans are barred from the ground by UEFA. No referee is named yet. I trim Sunderland's attacking numbers a little and cards slightly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 2.1 of them for Sunderland, and only take 3% off for their poor scoring lately (3 goals in 6). They know Hume is out but not that Brobbey, their main striker, and Xhaka, who runs their midfield, are both injured, plus a likely rotated side before Spurs; I go to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.6 corners, 7.2 for Sunderland, already a little lower for recent form. A rotated, Xhaka-less home side should still dominate the ball against a struggling Jagiellonia, so I trim only slightly, to about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.1 cards and already raise both sides for card-heavy runs (+7% and +8%). Jagiellonia lose their combative captain Romanczuk to a ban, and with no away fans the atmosphere should be calmer; no referee is named, so I trim slightly, to about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 28.6 shots, 21.3 for Sunderland, and add 8% for their busy recent shooting. Without Brobbey and Xhaka and with changes likely before Tottenham, I expect a little less volume, about 27.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 9.9 shots on target. Losing their main striker hurts accuracy more than volume and Sunderland have struggled to turn chances into goals lately, so I go to about 9.4.
